data.title: Four Philippine Air Force pilots killed in training accident
data.description:
Two Philippine Air Force trainer aircraft crashed during a training flight at an air base south of the capital Manila, killing four pilots, the military said on Saturday.

  • The aviation accident on Friday involved two SF-260 aircraft during a training flight at the Fernando Air Base in Batangas province, the Philippine Air Force said in a statement

  • Local media has reported the two planes collided in midair

  • The aircraft crashed within the grounds of the air base but there were no other casualties

  • The Air Force has temporarily grounded its fleet of SF-260 trainer planes pending an investigation into the cause of the accident

  • In May, two pilots were killed when an SF-260 trainer aircraft crashed in a mountainous area in northern Philippines, while another SF-260 TP Marchetti crashed during a 2023 training flight, also killing two pilots

  • The military used SF-260 aircraft during months of air strikes on southern Marawi City after militants loyal to Islamic State seized the area in 2017

data.title: Zymeworks Presents New Phase 1 Data for Folate Receptor Alpha-Targeting Antibody-Drug Conjugate ZW191 at ESMO Congress 2026
data.description:
Key points:
  • ZW191 demonstrates compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer across folate receptor alpha (FRα) expression levels
  • Confirmed objective response rates (cORR) of 64.5% at the 6.4 mg/kg dose in patients with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer
  • Median duration of response not yet reached at either dose level at median 7 months follow-up, with six-month progression-free survival rate of 61% in both groups
  • Favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, supports continued clinical development in partnership or through a strategic collaboration
  • Conference call with Zymeworks management on October 27 at 8:30 am Eastern Time (ET)

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zymeworks Inc. , a biotechnology company managing a portfolio of licensed healthcare assets while developing a diverse pipeline of novel, multifunctional biotherapeutics, today presented new clinical data from the randomized dose-optimization portion of its ongoing Phase 1 study evaluating ZW191, a FRα-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 in Madrid, Spain.

The presentation highlights compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC), including patients with high-grade serous disease across all levels of FRα expression. The results demonstrate compelling response rates, durability and a favorable tolerability profile, particularly at the 6.4 mg/kg dose, further supporting the potential of ZW191 to address limitations of currently available FRα-targeted therapies and expand treatment opportunities for patients with ovarian cancer.

“We are highly encouraged by these results, which further demonstrate the differentiated clinical profile of ZW191 and its potential to deliver meaningful benefit to patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer,” said Sabeen Mekan, M.D., Senior Vice President and Chief Medical Officer, Zymeworks. “The robust response rates observed at both doses, including meaningful activity in patients with low or negative FRα expression, reinforce the potential of ZW191 to benefit a broader patient population. Importantly, the encouraging durability of responses and favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, provide valuable insights to guide dose selection and the next stage of clinical development.”

The analysis included efficacy and safety data from 80 patients with PROC randomized to receive ZW191 at 6.4 mg/kg (n=37) or 9.6 mg/kg (n=43) every three weeks, as of the September 10, 2026 data cutoff date. Patients were heavily pretreated, having received a median of four prior lines of therapy, with 45% receiving five or more prior lines. Median follow-up was seven months. FRα expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry and categorized as low/negative (0%–24%), intermediate (25%–74%) or high (75%–100%) based on the percentage of tumor cells with 2+ or 3+ staining intensity.

Key Findings

Among response-evaluable patients with high-grade serous PROC, ZW191 demonstrated a cORR of 64.5% at 6.4 mg/kg and 55.3% at 9.6 mg/kg, with disease control rates of 100% and 92.1%, respectively. These findings demonstrate compelling anti-tumor activity at both doses in a heavily pretreated patient population.

ZW191 demonstrated meaningful anti-tumor activity across FRα expression in patients with high-grade serous PROC. Confirmed objective response rates were 69.2% in patients with high FRα expression, 50.0% in patients with intermediate FRα expression and 55.0% in patients with low or negative FRα expression. These findings support the potential of ZW191 to show improved efficacy than existing FRα targeted therapies in FRα high population and meaningfully benefit patients with lower expression who may not be eligible for currently approved FRα targeting therapies.

Responses to ZW191 were deep and durable, with median duration of response not yet reached at either dose. Six-month progression-free survival (PFS) was 61% in both groups, while median PFS was 7.9 months at 6.4 mg/kg and 9.8 months at 9.6 mg/kg in patients with high-grade serous PROC. At the time of data cutoff, 45% of patients remained on treatment, and PFS data continue to mature, especially at 6.4 mg/kg.

ZW191 continued to demonstrate a favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 22% of patients receiving 6.4 mg/kg compared with 44% at 9.6 mg/kg. Treatment-emergent adverse events leading to dose reductions occurred in 5% and 33% of patients, respectively, while discontinuations due to adverse events occurred in 14% and 19%. No deaths due to treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in either treatment group. The overall safety profile was manageable and supports continued clinical development.

“These results are particularly promising for patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer who have exhausted available treatment options,” said Jung-Yun Lee, M.D., Ph.D., Yonsei Cancer Center and Severance Hospital, Seoul, Republic of South Korea, and primary investigator who presented the results at ESMO 2026. “We observed substantial anti-tumor activity in patients who had received multiple prior therapies, including meaningful responses across high, intermediate and low or negative FRα expression levels. The encouraging durability of responses, together with the favorable safety profile observed at the lower dose, suggests ZW191 has the potential to become an important new treatment option for patients with this difficult-to-treat disease.”

The findings demonstrate encouraging anti-tumor activity across the 6.4 mg/kg and 9.6 mg/kg dose levels, with a more favorable tolerability profile at 6.4 mg/kg. These results will inform optimal dose selection for further clinical development.

ZW191's differentiated profile, including its novel FRα-targeting antibody, proprietary topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, ZD06519, and high drug-to-antibody ratio, supports its potential to address key limitations of existing therapies and broaden the applicability of FRα-targeted treatment approaches.

The presentation will be available on Zymeworks’ website at www.zymeworks.com/publications/.

Investor Call Details

Zymeworks invites investors and the general public to view and listen to a live webcast of its conference call with investment analysts at 8:30 am ET on October 27, 2026.

Dial-in details and webcast link are available on Zymeworks’ website at https://ir.zymeworks.com/events-and-presentations. A webcast replay of the call will be available on the Zymeworks website within 24 hours following the conclusion of the live call and will be archived for a limited period.

About ZW191

ZW191 is an antibody-drug conjugate engineered to target a protein called folate receptor-⍺ found in ~75% of high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas,1 over 50% of endometrial cancers,2,3 and ~70% of lung adenocarcinomas4. ZW191’s differentiated design strongly supports its ability to internalize into FR⍺-expressing cells with the potential to release bystander active topoisomerase-1 inhibitor (ZD06519), a novel proprietary payload developed by Zymeworks to kill tumor cells.

The Company has engaged MTS Healthcare to evaluate strategic partnering opportunities to fund further development for ZW191 with the objective of maximizing long-term value.

About Zymeworks Inc.

Zymeworks is a global biotechnology company building a diversified portfolio of healthcare assets designed to generate durable cash flows while advancing innovative medicines for difficult-to-treat diseases. The Company’s asset and royalty aggregation strategy combines a growing portfolio of commercial and near-commercial assets, including YUPELRI® (revefenacin), with a differentiated internal research and development engine. Zymeworks’ portfolio also includes Ziihera® (zanidatamab-hrii), a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody discovered and developed by Zymeworks and commercialized through global partnerships with Jazz Pharmaceuticals and BeOne Medicines, and pasritamig, a clinical-stage multispecific antibody developed by Johnson & Johnson using Zymeworks’ proprietary antibody engineering technologies.

Zymeworks is advancing a diverse pipeline of novel biotherapeutics, leveraging its proprietary Azymetric™ platform and expertise in antibody-drug conjugates, multispecific antibodies and other next-generation antibody technologies. These capabilities, together with Zymeworks’ integrated drug development expertise, enable the Company to develop differentiated therapeutics and create value through both internal innovation and strategic partnerships.

data.title: Immatics Presents Clinical Activity of IMA402 PRAME Bispecific and IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy across Advanced Solid Tumors in Two Oral Presentations at 2026 ESMO Annual Meeting
data.description:
Key points:
  • IMA402 PRAME bispecific continues to demonstrate encouraging anti-tumor activity in multiple indications, alongside a favorable safety profile
  • IMA402 achieved a cORR of 32%, 12.5 months median DOR and a 1-year OS rate of 91% in advanced melanoma patients with high PRAME expression
  • Clinical profile of IMA402 reinforces development path across multiple solid tumor indications, including melanoma, gynecologic cancers and lung cancer, in earlier and later treatment lines, supported by Immatics’ innovative, rapid liquid biopsy-based PRAME testing
  • IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy demonstrated deep and durable anti-tumor activity across multiple tumor types with a manageable safety profile, supporting its tumor-agnostic potential. At clinically relevant dose levels in patients with advanced, heavily pretreated gynecologic cancers, cORR was 55% with a median DOR of 8.4 months

Houston, Texas and Tuebingen, Germany, October 24, 2026 – Immatics N.V. (NASDAQ: IMTX, “Immatics” or the “Company”), the global leader in precision targeting of PRAME with multiple clinical-stage programs spanning cell therapies and bispecifics, today announced updated clinical trial data from its ongoing Phase 1b study with IMA402 PRAME bispecific and its Phase 1 study with IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy.

The IMA402 data will be presented in a rapid oral presentation (1955RO) by Dirk Schadendorf, M.D., and the IMA203CD8 data were presented in an oral presentation (1946O) by Antonia Busse, M.D., at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) in Madrid, Spain. In addition, exploratory analyses of the anzu-cel Phase 1b melanoma cohort will be presented in a poster (2128P) by Sapna Patel, M.D. The slides are available in the ‘Events & Presentations’ section of the Investor & Media page on the Company’s website.

“The data presented at ESMO further underscore the potential of IMA402 as an off-the-shelf treatment option for patients with solid cancers. This promising clinical profile reinforces our strategy as we continue to advance IMA402 across multiple cancer types and treatment lines, with combination approaches further expanding its reach,” said Cedrik Britten, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer at Immatics. “In addition, as the IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy data continue to mature, we are increasingly encouraged by its broad potential for patients with advanced PRAME-positive cancers. Together with anzu-cel, IMA402 and IMA203CD8 give us three distinct and complementary approaches to target PRAME, with the potential to reach more patients across a broad range of cancers.”

Rapid Oral Presentation Summary - IMA402 PRAME TCR Bispecific Phase 1b Trial

Patient Population: Heavily pretreated patient population with a median of 3 prior lines of therapy

As of the data cutoff on June 1, 2026, 126 heavily pretreated patients across multiple tumor types, primarily melanoma and ovarian cancer, received at least one infusion of IMA402 during the dose escalation or dose expansion part of the ongoing trial (NCT05958121). Patients had received a median of 3 prior lines of systemic treatment, had a median target lesion sum of diameter of 7.4 cm and had a median of 4 tumor lesions. The efficacy population included 40 patients treated within the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) range of 10 to 45 mg across varying levels of PRAME expression. Within this population, 31 patients exhibited high PRAME expression levels (PRAME-high)1 in their tumors. Of these, all patients with PRAME-high melanoma had received prior systemic treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), with a median of 2 prior ICI regimens and all patients with PRAME-high ovarian cancer were previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy.

Safety: Favorable tolerability profile as monotherapy and as combination therapy

IMA402 showed favorable tolerability across all doses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were expected, transient lymphopenia and low-grade cytokine release syndrome (CRS), consistent with the mechanism of action. No cases of ICANS were reported. No IMA402-related Grade 5 events were reported. Tolerability was consistent across all evaluated doses, including the RP2D range, with no additive toxicity observed when combined with an ICI.

Anti-tumor Activity and Durability: 32% cORR in PRAME-high melanoma with promising durability and survivalIMA402 showed promising anti-tumor activity as monotherapy (n=36) or in combination with an immune checkpoint inhibitor (n=4) in the efficacy population at RP2D range. Treatment with IMA402 demonstrated 10 confirmed responses resulting in an overall confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 25% (10/40) and a disease control rate (DCR) of 63% (25/40). This includes one confirmed complete response in melanoma. The longest ongoing response exceeded 2 years. In the PRAME-high population, cORR was 32% (10/31) across all indications and 32% (7/22) in patients with melanoma. The PRAME-high melanoma population further showed a median duration of response (mDOR) of 12.5 months (median follow-up, mFU, 16.8 months). Median overall survival (mOS) was not reached (mFU 8.8 months), with 91% of patients alive at 1 year (versus 60% of patients treated below RP2D range), indicating promising overall survival data irrespective of best response. Among 6 patients with PRAME-high ovarian cancer, 3 confirmed responses were reported.

Next Development Steps for IMA402:

The promising clinical profile of IMA402 supports a development path across various solid tumors in earlier and later treatment lines. These include combination approaches with ICIs in melanoma and in gynecologic cancers as well as IMA402 in combination with the Company’s MAGEA4/8-directed bispecific, IMA401, in lung cancer with first data expected in 2027. Furthermore, the use of Immatics’ proprietary rapid, sensitive and reliable liquid biopsy-based PRAME testing enables precise patient selection and could support potential fast-to-market strategies, subject to regulatory approval, in PRAME-high melanoma and beyond.

Oral Presentation Summary - IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy Phase 1 Trial

Patient population: Heavily pretreated patient population with limited treatment options

As of the data cutoff on August 7, 2026, 98 heavily pretreated patients across multiple advanced solid tumor types expressing PRAME that had undergone a median of 3 prior systemic treatments were enrolled in the ongoing Phase 1 dose escalation/dose expansion trial (NCT03686124). Of these, 90 patients were evaluable for efficacy, including 27 with gynecologic cancers (ovarian and uterine cancer), 44 with melanoma, 12 with synovial sarcoma and 7 with other solid tumor types. All patients with ovarian cancer had received prior platinum-based therapy.

Safety: Treatment with IMA203CD8 was manageable

IMA203CD8 demonstrated a consistent and manageable safety profile across different solid tumor types and a wide dose range (median dose 1.81x109 TCR T cells, range 0.44-12.50x109). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were expected and included transient cytopenias associated with the lymphodepletion regimen and low-grade cytokine release syndrome (CRS), consistent with the mechanism of action. ICANS was infrequently observed, and no IMA203CD8-related Grade 5 events occurred. Maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was not reached with doses up to 12.5 billion IMA203CD8 cells.

Anti-tumor Activity and Durability: One-time infusion of IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy showed anti-tumor activity across multiple tumor types

Across all evaluated dose levels and tumor types, including lower dose levels not selected for further clinical development, a one-time infusion of IMA203CD8 demonstrated an ORR of 51% (46/90) and a cORR of 41% (36/87). The DCR was 82% (74/90) and 83% (71/86) of patients with evaluable target lesions experienced tumor reduction. Responses were observed across multiple solid tumors expressing PRAME, including ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, melanoma, synovial sarcoma, and others. Durable long-term responses were observed with ongoing responses for more than 2.5 years.

In 20 patients with gynecologic cancers (ovarian and uterine cancer) treated at clinically relevant dose levels (≥DL4c), IMA203CD8 demonstrated consistent anti-tumor activity with an ORR of 60% (12/20) and a cORR of 55% (11/20), a DCR of 70% (14/20) and tumor reduction in 68% (13/19) of patients. Next Development Steps for IMA203CD8:

Phase 1a dose escalation is complete. Immatics is currently enrolling patients with uterine cancer at clinically relevant doses to further expand the clinical dataset in this indication. In addition, a Phase 1/2 investigator-initiated trial (IIT) in patients with PRAME-positive pediatric cancers is planned to start in 1H 2027. The clinical activity of IMA203CD8 observed across tumor types with distinct biology and differing levels of PRAME expression, including ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, melanoma and synovial sarcoma, supports the broad applicability of IMA203CD8 across PRAME-positive cancers. The development approach for IMA203CD8 will leverage targeted cohorts of selected tumor types, such as ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, rare cancers and pediatric cancers to build the clinical evidence base for broader, tumor-agnostic application.

Poster Presentation Summary – Anzu-cel Phase 1b Melanoma Cohort

Additional exploratory analyses (data cutoff Sept 24, 2025) of anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel, IMA203), presented in a poster (2128P) by Sapna Patel, M.D., demonstrated durable clinical benefit following a one-time treatment in a heavily pretreated population of patients with advanced melanoma. Durable clinical benefit was observed across patients with varied baseline clinical and treatment characteristics, with no single characteristic identified as a predictor of prolonged PFS. Exploratory analyses suggested that lower tumor burden, lower LDH, and a higher effector-to-target ratio may be associated with longer PFS. These findings further strengthen the clinical profile of anzu-cel, which is currently being evaluated in the Phase 3 SUPRAME trial in advanced melanoma.

About IMA402 PRAME Bispecific

IMA402 is a molecule from Immatics’ TCR bispecifics (TCER®) pipeline directed against an HLA-A*02:01-presented peptide derived from PRAME. IMA402 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1b clinical trial in patients with solid tumors expressing PRAME. IMA402 is part of Immatics’ strategy to leverage the full clinical potential of targeting PRAME, one of the most promising targets for TCR-based therapies.

About IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy

IMA203CD8 is Immatics’ PRAME-directed TCR T-cell therapy engineered to recognize an intracellular PRAME-derived peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on the cell surface and initiate a potent and specific anti-tumor response. Co-transduction of CD8αβ with the PRAME TCR adds functional CD4+ T cells designed to boost anti-tumor activity. IMA203CD8 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1b clinical trial in solid tumors expressing PRAME.

About Anzu-cel PRAME Cell Therapy

Anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel; IMA203) is a PRAME-directed TCR T-cell therapy engineered to recognize an intracellular PRAME-derived peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on the cell surface and initiate a potent and specific anti-tumor response. Anzu-cel PRAME cell therapy is currently being evaluated in a registration-enabling randomized controlled Phase 3 trial, “SUPRAME,” in patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma who have disease progression on or after treatment with at least one checkpoint inhibitor. In parallel, the Phase 1/2 clinical trial is ongoing with a focus on uveal melanoma.

About PRAME

PRAME is a tumor-associated target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Immatics’ PRAME franchise includes multiple product candidates, therapeutic modalities, indications and combination approaches: anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel; IMA203) and IMA203CD8, both PRAME-directed cell therapies, and IMA402, a PRAME-directed bispecific. Combination approaches include IMA402 with immune checkpoint inhibitors, IMA402 with the MAGEA4/8-directed bispecific IMA401, and anzu-cel in combination with Moderna’s PRAME mRNA therapy designed to enhance the cell therapy response.

Immatics is committed to making a meaningful impact on the lives of patients with cancer. We are the global leader in precision targeting of PRAME, a target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Our cutting-edge science and robust clinical pipeline form the broadest PRAME franchise with the most PRAME indications and modalities, spanning TCR T-cell therapies and TCR bispecifics.

data.title: S&P set to change how it classifies US growth and value stocks
data.description:
S&P Dow Jones Indices is changing how it classifies US stocks as growth or value, dropping share price momentum from its growth assessment and adding free cash flow to its value assessment.

The changes will affect indices such as the S&P 500 Growth and S&P 500 Value, along with corresponding indices tracking mid-cap and small-cap stocks. According to an S&P Dow Jones Indices release dated October 23, the revised rules will take effect on December 21, 2026, as part of its annual index reconstitution.

Under the current rules, S&P Dow Jones Indices assesses growth stocks using three factors: the change in earnings per share over three years relative to the current share price, three-year sales per share growth and share price momentum over 12 months.

Under the new rules, it will drop the momentum factor and use the other two measures to assess growth stocks.

The changes to the value framework are more extensive. S&P Dow Jones Indices will replace the traditional book value-to-price ratio with an adjusted measure that accounts for intangible assets.

Changes to S&P's growth and value factors

FactorBeforeAfter
Growth 1. Three-Year Net Change in Earnings per Share (Excluding Extra Items) over Current Price 2. Three-Year Sales per Share Growth Rate 3. Momentum (12-Month % Price Change)1. Three-Year Net Change in Earnings per Share (Excluding Extra Items) over Current Price 2. Three-Year Sales per Share Growth Rate
Value 1. Book Value to Price Ratio 2. Earnings to Price Ratio (trailing) 3. Sales to Price Ratio1. Intangibles-adjusted Book Value to Price 2. Earnings to Price Ratio (trailing) + Forward One-Year Earnings to Price Ratio (simple average blend of the two factors) 3. Sales to Price Ratio 4. Free Cash Flow to Price Ratio
S&P Dow Jones release - October 23

It will also combine trailing earnings-to-price with forward one-year earnings-to-price, using a simple average of the two. The sales-to-price ratio will remain, while free cash flow-to-price will be added as a new factor.

Free cash flow is the cash a company generates after accounting for capital spending. By adding this measure, the index provider will use another way to assess a company's value relative to its share price. However, the new free cash flow measure will not apply to real estate, banks, insurance and certain financial services industries. These sectors and industries will be assessed using the other value factors.

Clients will first see the changes in preliminary index files from December 4, before the revised indices take effect ahead of the market opening on December 21.

data.title: Darolutamide plus ADT and radiation therapy reduces risk of metastasis or death by 58% in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence
data.description:
ORION CORPORATION

PRESS RELEASE

24 OCTOBER 2026 at 9.35 EEST

Darolutamide plus ADT and radiation therapy reduces risk of metastasis or death by 58% in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence

  • Interim analysis results from the Phase 3 trial DASL-HiCaP show a 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death in the combined primary endpoint of metastasis-free survival (MFS-CI) with darolutamide versus placebo, in addition to androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and radiation therapy
  • Four-year metastasis-free survival rate in trial reached 95% with darolutamide compared to 88% with placebo, alongside secondary endpoint improvements and a safety profile consistent with previous studies
  • Results will be presented as a late-breaking abstract in a Presidential Symposium at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026

ESPOO, Finland, October 24, 2026 – New late-breaking data to be presented today at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 will show that adding darolutamide, an androgen receptor inhibitor (ARi) initially discovered by Orion Pharma, to standard-of-care androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and locoregional radiation therapy (RT), significantly improves metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI) in prostate cancer patients with high risk of recurrence compared to placebo. Darolutamide is currently not approved for this treatment setting. These data will be presented at Presidential Symposium I at the ESMO Congress 2026 (LBA4, Saturday 24 October, 16:30 CET).

At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the interim analysis demonstrated a 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death with darolutamide plus ADT and RT compared with placebo plus ADT and RT (hazard ratio [HR] 0.42; 95% CI: 0.27–0.66; p=0.0001). The 4-year metastasis-free survival rate was 95% for patients receiving darolutamide compared with 88% for those receiving placebo.

Secondary endpoints also showed consistent positive trends with darolutamide, with a 53% reduction in the risk of prostate-specific antigen progression free survival (PSA-PFS; HR 0.47; 95% CI: 0.33–0.67), and a 4-year PSA-PFS rate of 91% versus 83% with placebo. Prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS) and overall survival (OS) hazard ratios were 0.58 (95% CI: 0.17–1.97; 99% vs 99% at 4 years) and 0.88 (95% CI: 0.49–1.59; 97% vs 95% at 4 years), respectively, with follow-up ongoing.

The safety profile of darolutamide was consistent with its known tolerability, with adverse events being similar to the placebo group. Proportions of patients experiencing Grade ≥2 adverse events of special interest for darolutamide versus placebo were: fatigue/asthenia (14% vs 10%), hypertension (7% vs 9%), fractures (2% vs 3%), and cardiac events (3% vs 3%). Any Grade ≥3 adverse event occurred in 43% of patients in the darolutamide group versus 36% in the placebo group.

Follow-up of participants is continuing to provide further information on longer-term outcomes, including overall survival.

About the DASL-HiCaP trial (ANZUP1801)

The DASL-HiCaP trial is an investigator-initiated, randomized, placebo-controlled, Phase III trial (NCT04136353) evaluating darolutamide added to standard-of-care ADT and locoregional radiation therapy in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence. DASL-HiCaP is conducted by the University of Sydney and ANZUP Clinical Trials Group and is the fourth Phase III trial for darolutamide. Following ARAMIS, ARASENS, and ARANOTE, which demonstrated darolutamide’s efficacy and safety in advanced prostate cancer, DASL-HiCaP represents the first Phase III study of darolutamide in early prostate cancer. A total of 1,106 participants across Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United States, Ireland and the United Kingdom were randomized 1:1 to receive darolutamide (600 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 96 weeks, combined with an LHRH analog for 96 weeks and RT to the prostate/prostate bed and pelvic lymph nodes. The primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS CI). Secondary endpoints included prostate-specific antigen progression free survival (PSA-PFS), prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS), and overall survival (OS). The protocol specified an interim analysis after 87 MFS-CI events; follow-up is ongoing to evaluate long-term overall survival.

About Prostate Cancer

Prostate cancer is the second most common cancer and the fourth most common cause of cancer death in men worldwide. Over 1.5 million men are diagnosed with prostate cancer each year and almost 420,000 die from the disease worldwide. By 2040, prostate cancer diagnoses are projected to increase to 2.9 million.

Standard therapy for prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence combines radiation therapy with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). However, despite this approach, a significant proportion of patients experience treatment failure, local recurrence, or distant metastases. Intensifying therapy early with an advanced androgen receptor inhibitor aims to improve long-term disease control and delay metastatic progression.

About darolutamide (Nubeqa™)

Darolutamide is an oral ARi with a unique chemical structure that binds with high affinity to the androgen receptor and exhibits a strong antagonistic effect against the androgen receptor inhibiting the receptor function and growth of prostate cancer cells. Additionally, preclinical models and neuroimaging data in healthy humans, support darolutamide's low potential for blood-brain barrier penetration and low potential for clinically relevant drug drug interactions.

Darolutamide, under the brand name Nubeqa™ plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), is already approved in more than 85 markets around the world, including the US, EU and China. It is approved for the treatment of adult patients with mHSPC without docetaxel in 75 markets and with docetaxel in more than 85 countries, and for adult patients with nmCRPC at high risk of developing metastatic disease in more than 85 countries.

Darolutamide is developed jointly by Orion Pharma and Bayer.

A robust clinical development program is underway investigating darolutamide across various stages of prostate cancer. Current ongoing trials include the Phase III ARASTEP trial evaluating the efficacy of darolutamide plus ADT compared to ADT alone in hormone sensitive prostate cancer (HSPC), in patients with high-risk biochemical recurrence (BCR) who have no evidence of metastatic disease by conventional imaging and a positive PSMA PET/CT at baseline.

data.title: Firstwork Raises $15 Mn In Series A Round Led By Earlybird Venture Capital
data.description:
US-based HR tech startup plans to expand its AI-led workforce automation platform across the US and Europe, with 80 per cent of its workforce based in Bengaluru

US-based HR technology startup Firstwork has raised USD 15 million (over Rs 142 crore) in a Series A funding round led by Earlybird Venture Capital to expand its AI-powered workforce automation platform across the US and Europe, as per a media report.

The round also saw participation from Legion VC and Deel Ventures, alongside existing investors Gradient and Y Combinator. The latest fundraise takes Firstwork’s total funding to USD 20 million since its launch in 2024.

The San Francisco-based startup plans to use the capital to expand its teams across applied AI, AI research, engineering and go-to-market functions. Around 80 per cent of its workforce operates from Bengaluru. The company also plans to strengthen its presence in the US and Europe and extend its AI agents to additional workforce operations.

Founded by former Deel executives Vardhan Kapoor and Shubham Choudhary, Firstwork uses AI agents to automate human resource operations for frontline workers. Its platform covers document verification, background checks, right-to-work checks, onboarding, training coordination, compliance management and worker follow-ups.

The platform integrates with existing HR systems, allowing employers to automate workflows without replacing their current software.

According to the company, more than 1.5 lakh frontline workers start work through its platform every month. Firstwork claims its technology can reduce the time spent by workers and HR teams on each new hire by up to 90 per cent. Its clients include Deel, Job&Talent, Relay, Wonolo and BGSF.

The fundraise comes amid increasing adoption of artificial intelligence across human resource functions. India's HR technology market is projected to grow to USD 2.3 billion by 2033 from USD 1.12 billion in 2024, according to industry estimates.

Several Indian startups are developing AI-based solutions for recruitment, onboarding and workforce management. Bengaluru-based Hunar.AI, which raised Rs 40 crore earlier this week, uses conversational AI agents to automate gig-worker hiring, onboarding, training and employee retention. Its clients include Swiggy, Zepto, Croma, Starbucks and Dr Lal PathLabs.

Hyderabad-based TurboHire raised USD 6 million in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures in August 2025 to expand its agentic AI-based recruitment platform. Founded in 2019, the startup automates enterprise hiring workflows and says it has onboarded more than 120 enterprises, including Cipla, Tata Motors, PwC, Lenskart and Britannia.

Other companies operating in adjacent segments include TraqCheck, which offers AI-powered background verification and recruitment agents, and HireBound, which automates candidate sourcing, screening and evaluation.

data.title: IDBI Bank Unions Back Nationwide Strike Against Stake Sale
data.description:
UFBU backs the November 2–3 protest over the proposed Fairfax deal, citing concerns over public ownership and employee safeguards

IDBI Bank employees are set to stage a two-day nationwide strike on November 2 and 3, opposing the proposed sale of the bank to Canadian investor Fairfax Financial Holdings, with the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) extending support to the agitation.

In a circular dated October 22, the UFBU urged its affiliated unions and members to participate in solidarity programmes, backing the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees’ campaign against the proposed sale of a 60% stake held by the government and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC).

The UFBU has questioned the proposed transfer of ownership and management control to a foreign investor, arguing that it raises concerns over the bank’s public-sector character. It has also cited a parliamentary assurance made in 2003 that the government would retain at least a 51% stake in IDBI.

The employee forum has demanded that the government halt the transaction and acquire an additional 6% equity in the bank, either from LIC or through market purchases, to maintain majority ownership. It has also sought written assurances that existing service conditions, welfare measures, pension benefits and reservation policies will be protected, along with the continuation of industry-level wage revisions.

As part of its solidarity campaign, the UFBU has called for participation in demonstrations and a social media campaign, besides other protest activities ahead of the strike.

The proposed agitation comes as the government moves to divest its stake in IDBI Bank, a lender that the unions say has returned to profitability in recent years. The strike is intended to press for a reconsideration of the proposed transaction and safeguards for employees.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Says Refiners See 'High Probability' Of Sharp Oil Supply Drop As Houthi Attacks Escalate — Crude Oil Prices Hit 6-Month High
data.description:
Key points:
  • According to Struyven, refiners are among those buying more crude because of the intensification of shipping attacks and strikes on infrastructure by the Houthis.
  • Crude oil prices rose to a six-month high, with the U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures expiring in December rising 4.46% to $103.44 a barrel after a 7.81% gain the week before.
  • Brent crude futures expiring in December rose 6.24% this week, hovering around $116.93 a barrel after a 4.91% increase the week before.

Crude oil prices have climbed to a six-month high as escalating attacks and rising tensions in the Middle East add to concerns about energy supply disruptions.

The latest escalation comes as fighting involving the Iran-aligned Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition has intensified, while shipping incidents have added to concerns around key waterways used to transport oil.

Goldman Sachs' co-head of Global Commodities Research and head of Oil Research, Daan Struyven, said the recent rise in crude prices reflects growing downside risks to supply, with physical buyers and investors both contributing to the stronger market.

Crude Oil Prices Hit Six-Month High

Crude oil prices rose to a six-month high, with the U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures expiring in December rising 4.46% to $103.44 a barrel after a 7.81% gain the week before. Brent crude futures expiring in December rose 6.24% this week, hovering around $116.93 a barrel after a 4.91% increase the week before.

The United States Oil Fund ETF (USO) rose more than 4% on Friday, while the ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil ETF (UCO) gained about 4%.

Goldman Sachs Sees Growing Downside Risks To Oil Supply

Struyven said Brent crude had risen sharply as growing Middle East tensions and increasing downside risks to supply prompted buyers to bid up barrels in both physical and financial markets.

According to Struyven, refiners are among those buying more crude because of the intensification of shipping attacks and strikes on infrastructure by the Houthis. With inventories low, physical buyers are trying to secure barrels while they remain available.

Struyven said refiners see a "high probability of a sharp drop in supply," helping explain the precautionary buying taking place in the physical oil market.

He also pointed to financial-market demand, saying investors are buying oil as a hedge against higher energy prices because bonds and equities have become unusually sensitive to movements in crude.

Goldman Sachs sees the risks to oil prices as increasingly symmetrical following the recent surge, although Struyven said risks to the firm's forecasts remain skewed to the upside.

The bank's base case calls for Brent to end this year at $90 a barrel and average $80 a barrel in 2027. Struyven identified an intensification of shipping attacks, damage to oil infrastructure and a more persistent risk premium as key upside risks.

The analyst highlighted that crude oil exports from the Persian Gulf had reached about 110% of 2025 average levels over the previous couple of weeks, while refined-product exports such as diesel were running at only about 40% of the 2025 average.

He attributed part of the disparity to damage to refineries in the Middle East and the greater difficulty of arranging ship-to-ship transfers for refined products.

Goldman Sachs also sees factors beyond the Middle East supporting refined-product prices. Struyven pointed to structural tightness stemming from years of underinvestment, as well as reduced diesel production at Russian refineries following Ukrainian drone attacks.

Houthi Attacks Add To Middle East Supply Concerns

Tensions around key Middle East shipping routes have intensified in recent weeks, with attacks involving the Iran-aligned Houthis adding to concerns over the movement of oil and other energy products.

According to a Reuters report, Saudi Aramco ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran on Thursday, as fighting intensified between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. Dhahran is located near Bahrain and is home to the headquarters of the world's largest crude oil exporter.

Separately, an oil spill was detected off the coast of Umm Al Quwain in the United Arab Emirates, according to the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment. The ministry did not say what caused the spill, and authorities had not identified the tanker involved.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, rose 0.15%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) edged up by 0.07%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) gained 0.13%. data.title: CCPA Imposes Rs 1 Lakh Penalty On Britannia Over 100% Whole Wheat Bread’ Claim
data.description:
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of Rs 1 lakh on Britannia Industries Ltd. for misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices concerning its ‘100% Whole Wheat Bread’ product. The authority has directed the company to discontinue the advertisements with immediate effect and submit a compliance report within 15 days.

In an order dated October 22, 2026, the CCPA held that the prominent ‘100% Whole Wheat Bread’ claim was misleading because the product contained only 62% whole wheat flour, while the remaining 38% comprised other ingredients, including water, yeast, wheat bran and other constituents.

The authority concluded that the claim conveyed the impression that the product consisted entirely of whole wheat flour, contrary to its actual composition. It also held that the accompanying ‘0% Maida’ claim did not cure or mitigate the misleading impression.

CCPA Rejects Britannia’s Defence

The proceedings arose from suo motu cognizance taken by the CCPA over Britannia’s product packaging and advertisements across its website and social media platforms.

Following a preliminary inquiry, the authority issued a notice to the company on January 13, 2025. Britannia submitted its response on January 28, 2025, arguing that the claim referred to the composition of the flour used in the product rather than the composition of the finished bread.

The company maintained that the product contained 62% whole wheat flour and that the remaining ingredients were necessary for manufacturing bread. It also contended that the expression ‘100% Whole Wheat Flour’ was calculated on a flour basis and that the claim was intended to communicate the absence of refined flour or maida.

The CCPA subsequently examined an investigation report dated September 7, 2026, received from the Director General (Investigation), along with findings and observations furnished by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI).

According to the order, the FSSAI observed that the use of ‘100%’ in isolation or in conjunction with descriptors could create a false impression of absolute purity or superiority. The investigation also found that the product’s whole wheat flour content was below the prescribed threshold for using the nomenclature ‘Whole Wheat Bread’.

FSSAI Standards And The 75% Threshold

The CCPA referred to Regulation 2.6 of the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Second Amendment Regulations, 2022, which stipulates that whole wheat flour must constitute at least 75% of the prescribed composition for a product to be displayed as ‘Whole Wheat Bread’.

The authority noted that Britannia’s product contained 62% whole wheat flour, below the prescribed threshold. It rejected the company’s argument that the claim should be assessed exclusively on a flour basis, holding that the overall composition and presentation of the finished product were relevant to determining whether consumers were misled.

The order further recorded that the FSSAI had issued an advisory dated May 28, 2025, advising food business operators to discontinue the use of the term ‘100%’ on food product labels, packaging and promotional materials.

The CCPA also noted that, according to the investigation findings, Britannia continued displaying the claim on its website and promotional channels despite the advisory and subsequent regulatory communications.

CCPA Finds Disclaimer Insufficient

The authority observed that the product’s front packaging prominently displayed ‘100% Whole Wheat Bread’, alongside the ‘0% Maida’ claim. A qualifying statement on the reverse side read: ‘Made from 100% Whole Wheat Flour on Flour Basis’.

The CCPA held that the disclaimer, linked to the front-label claim through a symbol and presented in comparatively small print, did not adequately correct the impression created by the prominent claim.

It observed that an ordinary consumer might not examine the detailed ingredient declaration before purchasing the product. The authority also found that the placement and presentation of the qualification made it insufficiently prominent to clarify the actual composition.

The CCPA further considered the accompanying representation that the bread ‘pairs perfectly well with a healthy diet’, holding that the overall packaging could create an impression about the product’s dietary suitability that was not adequately substantiated by its composition.

Findings Under The Consumer Protection Act, 2019

The CCPA held that the representations violated Section 2(28) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which defines misleading advertisements, and constituted an unfair trade practice under Section 2(47).

The authority also referred to Section 2(9), concerning consumer rights, including the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price of goods.

In addition, the order referred to Regulation 4(1) of the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018, and the Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements and Endorsements for Misleading Advertisements, 2022.

The CCPA concluded that the prominent numerical claim, combined with the limited prominence of the qualifying disclosure, misrepresented the product’s composition and could influence consumers’ purchasing decisions.

Exercising its powers under Sections 10, 18, 20 and 21 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the CCPA issued the following directions to Britannia Industries Ltd.:

1. Discontinuation of advertisements: Immediately discontinue the false and misleading advertisements across print and electronic media, including social media.

2. Monetary penalty: Pay a penalty of Rs 1,00,000 for engaging in misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices.

3. Compliance report: Submit a report to the CCPA on compliance with the directions within 15 days from the date of the order.

The order reinforces the CCPA’s position that food-product claims must be assessed in the context of the product’s actual composition and the overall impression conveyed to an ordinary consumer. It also underscores that a qualifying statement in fine print may not be sufficient to neutralise a prominent, potentially misleading claim on product packaging.

data.title: Coal Gasification Can Cut Import Dependence, But Costs Remain A Hurdle
data.description:
Jindal Steel highlights up to 90 per cent domestic sourcing for new gasification equipment, while industry experts flag high-ash Indian coal, project economics and carbon management as key considerations for commercial deployment

India’s coal gasification ambitions will depend on lowering capital costs, strengthening domestic equipment manufacturing and integrating carbon management solutions, industry executives said at Gasification India 2026 in New Delhi, as the country seeks to reduce dependence on imported industrial inputs and make greater use of domestic coal resources.

Speaking at the 17th edition of the conference, held on 22-23 October, Naveen Ahlawat, Head – Green Hydrogen, Green Steel, Gasification Projects and CCSU at Jindal Steel Limited, said the company’s experience with coal gasification highlighted the importance of supply-chain localisation and technology optimisation in making projects commercially viable.

Ahlawat said Jindal Steel had reduced its dependence on imported equipment and components for its ongoing gasification expansion, with domestic sourcing now accounting for around 90 per cent  of requirements, compared with approximately 55 per cent when the earlier plant was developed. “Cost is super important. The project cost, and everybody is aware that the growth of this project is capital expenditure-heavy. Optimisation, localisation of the supply chain, and reducing the cost are super important,” he said.

Domestic Manufacturing

Ahlawat said the company was applying lessons from its existing coal gasification operations to a new phase of development, including manufacturing gasifiers and associated equipment within India. The initiative also involves using steel plates produced at its own steel plant and working with domestic suppliers to reduce dependence on imported components. He said the company was also evaluating changes to gas purification technology to bring down investment requirements.

According to Ahlawat, replacing the Rectisol process with pressure swing adsorption (PSA) for syngas-based direct reduced iron production could substantially reduce costs where the more complex purification process is unnecessary. The localisation push comes as India explores coal gasification for producing synthesis gas, or syngas, a mixture primarily comprising hydrogen and carbon monoxide. Syngas can serve as an industrial feedstock and reducing agent in steelmaking, while also supporting the production of chemicals and other industrial products.

Ahlawat said coal gasification could help reduce exposure to imported industrial inputs, but stressed that project developers must assess coal characteristics, technology maturity, conversion efficiency and the value of by-products before committing capital. He also pointed to opportunities to use syngas in existing industrial processes, including blast furnaces and galvanising and colour-coating lines, potentially reducing the consumption of other fuels.

Carbon Management Challenge

However, the commercial case for coal gasification cannot be separated from its emissions profile, particularly as steelmakers face increasing pressure to decarbonise production. Ahlawat said gasification should be viewed as a transitional step rather than a substitute for the eventual shift towards green hydrogen and lower-carbon industrial processes. He cautioned that without integration with renewable energy and carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS), coal gasification’s carbon intensity could remain comparable to conventional coal-based processes.

“Gasification has to be looked at as a bridge fuel or as a bridge step,” he said, adding that the longer-term direction for the steel sector remained lower-carbon production.

Hidayatullah Mohammad, Senior Engineer – Gasification Technology at Air Products, said the quality of Indian coal presented a significant technical and economic challenge because of its high ash content and the resulting demands on gasification systems. An internal assessment by Air Products, cited by Mohammad, found that increasing coal ash content from 16 per cent to 32 per cent raised coal consumption by around 34-35 per cent and oxygen consumption by approximately 20 per cent to produce the same quantity of syngas. Mohammad said technology selection and reactor design therefore needed to account for local coal characteristics, ash behaviour and the economics of operating the plant.

“It will never be a technology limitation to handle any challenging coal. We just have to see what is the right economic model that can fit in, and we have to choose the right design basis for that,” he said. Vartika Shukla, former Chairman and Managing Director of Engineers India Limited, chaired the session on advancing coal gasification technologies for commercial deployment. The discussions highlighted the central challenge facing India’s gasification strategy: translating domestic resource availability into commercially competitive industrial production while limiting emissions and reducing dependence on imported technology and equipment.

Sonali Chawhan

BW Reporters The author is a Trainee Correspondent at BW Businessworld.

data.title: India’s Coal Gasification Push Faces Financing And Cost Hurdles, Industry Leaders Say
data.description:
India’s target of gasifying 100 million tonnes of coal annually will depend on project execution, reliable feedstock supplies and long-term purchase agreements, industry leaders said at Gasification India 2026

India’s coal gasification ambitions will require stronger financing mechanisms, assured demand and coordinated project execution to translate policy support into commercially viable investments, industry leaders said at the 17th edition of Gasification India 2026 in New Delhi on 22 October.

The two-day conference, being held on 22–23 October, brought together policymakers, coal producers, project developers, technology providers and investors to discuss the commercial deployment of coal and lignite gasification. The discussions come as India seeks to reduce import dependence, strengthen domestic manufacturing and expand the industrial use of indigenous coal resources.

Ashwinkumar Khatri, Director General of Mission Energy Foundation and organiser of the conference, said the priority was to move beyond policy commitments and address the financial, technological and operational barriers facing projects. He said financing, feedstock quality and offtake arrangements would be critical to building a competitive domestic coal gasification ecosystem.

Financing And Offtake Remain Key Hurdles

Amrit Lal Meena, Chairman of the Gasification Technologies & Research Council of India and former Secretary of the Ministry of Coal, identified four priorities for improving investor confidence: long-term financing, assured offtake, reliable feedstock supplies and faster project implementation. He said government support through capital incentives and coal availability had created opportunities for the sector, but projects would need predictable financial and commercial arrangements to become viable. Meena called for measures such as credit guarantees, repayment moratoria and timely disbursement of incentives. Recognising eligible coal gasification projects as infrastructure under the National Infrastructure Pipeline could also improve access to affordable financing, he said.

Long-term purchase agreements with the fertiliser, gas, chemicals and steel industries would help developers secure demand. Transparent offtake guarantees and price-stabilisation mechanisms could provide additional support to early projects. He also stressed the need for enforceable coal supply agreements covering quantity, quality, pricing and delivery, alongside adequate water, power and transport infrastructure.

Meena said the first group of integrated projects required coordinated assistance for land acquisition, statutory clearances and financial support. India aims to gasify 100 million tonnes of coal annually, with timely execution and investor confidence emerging as important factors in meeting the target.

Coal India Projects Move Ahead

Peeyush Kumar, Managing Director of BCGCL, the Coal India–Bharat Heavy Electricals joint venture, said construction had begun on three coal gasification projects being undertaken by Coal India and its partners. The projects involve collaborations with Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL), GAIL India and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL). Kumar said controlling project costs, strengthening engineering, procurement and construction capabilities, and improving project management would be essential to implementation. He also highlighted the potential of coal gasification to support import substitution, particularly in urea production.

However, reducing the ash content of Indian coal through washing would need greater policy attention to contain costs and improve the economics of initial projects. Kumar called for wider investor participation, exploration of new products and stronger cooperation among stakeholders. Separately, Alvarez & Marsal unveiled its report, Coal Gasification for ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ – Shaping the Next Industrial Revolution, at the conference. The event’s organisers said a policy paper would be prepared based on the conference discussions, with recommendations to be taken up with the government. The proposals are expected to focus on addressing implementation barriers and accelerating the development of India’s coal gasification sector.

Sonali Chawhan

data.title: Nomura Favours ACME Solar As Storage Gains Importance In India’s Clean Energy Market
data.description:
The brokerage assigns a Buy rating to ACME Solar and a Neutral rating to NTPC Green Energy, citing storage opportunities, project execution and transmission constraints

Nomura has picked ACME Solar Holdings as its preferred renewable energy play over NTPC Green Energy, betting on the growing value of battery storage and round-the-clock power supply as India scales up clean energy capacity.

The Japanese brokerage initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 505 for ACME Solar, while assigning NTPC Green Energy a Neutral rating and a target price of Rs 100. The contrasting assessments highlight a growing divide in India’s clean energy market: developers are increasingly being evaluated not only on planned renewable capacity but also on their ability to commission projects, integrate storage and deliver electricity when demand peaks.

India’s renewable energy capacity has expanded rapidly, but intermittent solar and wind generation has created challenges for grid management. Surplus solar power during the day and higher electricity demand outside solar hours have strengthened the case for battery energy storage systems (BESS) and firm, dispatchable renewable energy projects. According to market reports, the share of grid-storage-backed tenders rose from 22 per cent in financial year 2021–22 to 87 per cent in 2025–26, underlining the increasing importance of storage in renewable energy procurement.

Storage Strengthens ACME Solar’s Growth Outlook

Nomura expects ACME Solar’s revenue to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 66 per cent and earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) at 65 per cent between FY27 and FY29. The brokerage expects the company to add 4.3 gigawatts (GW) of contracted capacity during the period. The company is transitioning from a conventional solar independent power producer to a platform offering firm and dispatchable renewable power. More than half of its portfolio capacity is linked to firm and dispatchable renewable energy projects, which combine generation with storage to meet specified electricity supply schedules.

ACME Solar’s total portfolio stood at around 8.4 GW, including a recently awarded 300 MW project. Of this, approximately 3 GW was operational, while projects under execution provided further growth potential. Falling battery costs and early commissioning of storage assets could also improve project economics. Bringing storage online ahead of scheduled project completion can allow developers to monetise electricity through merchant and short-term markets, while improving returns on invested equity.

Transmission Constraints Cloud NTPC Green’s Prospects

Nomura expects NTPC Green Energy’s revenue and EBITDA to grow at CAGRs of 74 per cent and 72 per cent, respectively, between FY27 and FY29. The projections are supported by planned capacity additions, an extensive project pipeline and the parent company NTPC’s execution experience and relatively low borrowing costs. NTPC Green has approximately 12.9 GW of capacity under construction through its wholly owned subsidiary and another 3.4 GW under joint ventures. The company is targeting 60 GW of renewable energy capacity by FY32. However, Nomura has flagged transmission availability as a key risk, warning that connectivity constraints could delay project commissioning and limit capacity additions compared with the company’s guidance.

The broader investment trend suggests that India’s renewable energy expansion is entering a more execution-sensitive phase. As storage becomes integral to power procurement, access to transmission infrastructure, battery costs and commissioning schedules are likely to influence developers’ earnings visibility and capital efficiency. For investors, the distinction between announced capacity and operational assets remains critical, particularly as renewable developers compete to deliver dependable electricity rather than generation capacity alone.

data.title: Uno Minda Targets Rs 40,000 Cr Revenue By FY30 On EV Push
data.description:
The auto component maker plans to expand its electric vehicle powertrain, seating, sunroof and advanced electronics businesses as it looks to capitalise on vehicle electrification and rising demand for premium features

Uno Minda is targeting nearly double its revenue to Rs 40,000 crore by financial year 2030, banking on electric vehicle (EV) powertrains, complete seating systems, sunroofs and advanced electronics to drive its next phase of growth. The auto component manufacturer plans to expand its product portfolio and manufacturing capabilities as automakers increase investments in electrification, technology and premium vehicle features. The company’s revenue stood at around Rs 19,700 crore in FY26, according to media reports. Its growth strategy reflects a broader shift in India’s automotive component industry, where suppliers are seeking to increase the value of components supplied per vehicle rather than relying solely on growth in vehicle production volumes.

EV Investments Drive Expansion

Uno Minda is expanding its presence in electric-drive systems and other technology-intensive automotive components as manufacturers adapt to changing powertrain requirements. Its plans also cover seating systems, sunroofs and electronic features, which are gaining importance as passenger vehicles become more technologically advanced. The company’s expansion comes amid growing demand for EV-related components and increasing localisation of automotive technologies in India. It has also pursued technology partnerships and capacity additions to strengthen its position across conventional and electric vehicle platforms.

For FY27, Uno Minda has outlined capital expenditure of approximately Rs 1,750 crore, covering growth projects and investments required to maintain existing operations. Several manufacturing projects are expected to begin production or ramp up during the year, according to company updates. The strategy is aimed at diversifying revenue streams while strengthening its relationships with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). Higher component value per vehicle, product innovation and export opportunities could support growth beyond overall vehicle sales.

Premium Features Lift Prospects

The expansion also reflects the growing importance of premiumisation in India's passenger vehicle market. Features such as advanced lighting, infotainment systems, sunroofs and integrated seating solutions are becoming important areas of competition among automakers, creating opportunities for component suppliers. Industry analysts note that suppliers able to combine technology development, local manufacturing and product diversification may benefit from this shift. However, the pace of growth will depend on new plant utilisation, customer demand, project execution and the ability to manage rising input and labour costs.

The EV transition also presents a longer-term opportunity for component makers to move into higher-value products, including electric-drive units, controllers and related electronic systems. At the same time, capital-intensive expansion can put pressure on margins before new facilities reach optimal utilisation. For Uno Minda, achieving its FY30 revenue ambition will therefore depend not only on India's vehicle market expansion but also on converting investments and order wins into sustained sales. Its ability to scale newer businesses while maintaining profitability will remain a key factor in determining whether its technology-led growth strategy delivers the targeted results.

data.title: “We Will Focus On Increasing Make In India Lines For Women”: Casio MD
data.description:
Takuto Kimura says the company plans to introduce new locally manufactured watch models in 2027 as it seeks to double women’s watch sales by expanding its product portfolio

Casio India sees scope to double women’s watch sales by expanding its locally manufactured portfolio, developing new models across watch categories and capitalising on demand for fashion-led timepieces. The Japanese watchmaker is also looking to strengthen its brand presence and widen its retail reach, including in smaller cities and banking on demand for traditional watches among younger consumers.

“We will especially try to focus on increasing the Make in India line-ups and focus on the women's line-up…if we strengthen our strategy and product line-up in the women market, I'm confident that we can increase the sales double,” Takuto Kimura, Managing Director, Casio India, said in an interview with BW Businessworld on the sidelines of the Launch of G-Shock 2500 series.

The company has not disclosed the current contribution of women's watches to its Indian sales, a timeline for doubling the segment's sales or a quantified investment plan. Kimura said strengthening the product range and market strategy would be central to pursuing the opportunity, with additional India-made models potentially arriving in 2027.

Casio introduced a range of 28 locally manufactured watch models in January 2026, including 23 designs aimed at women, according to previously reported company announcements. The next phase of product development could include additions under G-Shock and Edifice, and other segments also, although the company has not confirmed launch dates or the number of models planned.

Casio reported double-digit sales growth for both G-Shock and its Casio Watch brand. Its results briefing said Casio Watch attracted new users, including women and younger consumers, and identified marketing to women as part of its strategy. The company also said demand for smartwatches appeared to have passed its peak.

Additionally, Casio India's revenue more than doubled to Rs 894 crore in FY25 from Rs 394 crore in FY21, while net profit rose to Rs 53.6 crore from Rs 8.3 crore over the same period, according to regulatory filings accessed through business intelligence platform Tofler.

Traditional Watches Remain Priority

Casio India is not currently planning to enter the smartwatch segment, despite the category's earlier rapid expansion. Kimura said the company would continue to focus on traditional watches, keeping its domestic strategy centred on established product categories rather than adding smartwatch offerings.

“As of now we focus on traditional watch,” Kimura said.

India's smartwatch market has contracted for two consecutive years, according to International Data Corporation (IDC). Shipments fell 17.6 per cent to 28.9 million units in 2025. In April-June 2026, shipments declined 4 per cent to 6.38 million units, marking the tenth consecutive quarter of contraction, although the decline was narrower than the 28.4 per cent fall recorded a year earlier.

The slowdown has not been uniform across the wider watch industry. Titan Company reported 23 per cent growth in its watches division in the June quarter of FY27, according to its business update. Analogue watches grew in the high twenties, while its smartwatch business declined in the low teens, highlighting the contrasting performance of traditional and connected timepieces.

“The young generation in India more tends to have a watch. Not only just timekeeping but also they try to wear it to express their own style and fashion,” he said.

He identified G-Shock as a brand that resonates with younger consumers who follow global trends in fashion, art, music and sport through social media. Casio Vintage, meanwhile, has benefited from interest in 1990s fashion, he said.

In India, Casio attributed continued G-Shock growth partly to the impact of two major brand ambassadors. Sales of Casio Watch also remained strong as its distributor network expanded beyond major cities into smaller urban markets. India and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations together accounted for 16 per cent of Casio's timepiece sales in the quarter; the company did not provide a separate India figure.

Casio India's immediate priorities remain watches, calculators and electronic musical instruments. Kimura said the company had no current plans to launch its earU hearing-assistance earbuds in India.

Retail Expansion Across India

Alongside product development, Casio India plans to increase its physical retail presence and strengthen online sales. The company had 85 brand stores at the time of the interview, Kimura said, as it seeks to build its reach across major cities and smaller markets. The company has a target to open 200 stores by 2030 and, with the ambition to double its India business over five years, Shin Takano, the company’s global CEO, has said previously.

“One of the key strategies we have to focus on is how to increase the number of brand stores nationwide in India…So from tier 1, we try to open a new flagship brand store. And tier 2, we expand the number of brand stores,” Kimura said, adding that while continuing to consider opportunities in tier 3 cities. At the same time, online sales would remain another area of focus.

Kimura said online and offline sales of watches were broadly comparable, although he did not provide a detailed channel-wise breakdown or distinguish between sales through Casio's own website and third-party ecommerce platforms.

In a September 2025, Kimura said Casio held a 12 per cent share of India's watch market, ranking second, compared with 8 per cent in 2014. He also outlined an ambition to triple sales by 2035. These figures were company-reported claims and were not independently established in the latest interview.

Competition In Women's Watches

Men's watches account for an estimated 57.68 per cent of India's watch market, while women's watches are the fastest-growing segment, with estimated growth of 9.16 per cent, according to Mordor Intelligence. The figures point to an opportunity for brands to broaden their appeal among women, although the estimates depend on the research firm's market definitions and forecast period.

Casio India is looking to strengthen its presence in the segment through product development and local manufacturing. Its women's portfolio will span categories including G-Shock and Edifice, Kimura said, as the company seeks to address a gap in its existing range.

“I think the women's category, of course some other brands have more line-up than Casio. However, as I said, the women market now has a big potential, so we strengthen this market,” he said.

Casio faces competition from established watchmakers and brands with dedicated women's collections. Titan's Raga range, alongside offerings from Fossil and Citizen, gives consumers alternatives designed around women's styling preferences. Casio's challenge is to expand its range and strengthen its relevance in a segment where competitors already have established product offerings.

Kimura said Indian consumers consider both price and brand value when choosing watches, although the importance of price varies across market segments. Casio's strategy is to build brand recognition through marketing while pricing products to suit their intended consumers. He did not provide a breakdown of sales or profitability for women's watches.

Priyanshu Priya

BW Reporters The author is trainee correspondent at BW Businessworld.

data.title: Japan Joins the Data Center Rush. These Stocks Can Benefit. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Craig Mellow

While the rest of the world frets about a data center hangover, financial and political, Japan is rushing to join the party. That could boost some stocks that have flown below radar.

A conservative Japan Inc. largely sat out the rush to cloud computing that powered Data Centers 1.0, preferring to keep information on their own servers, says Hisashi Arakawa, head of Japan equities at Aberdeen Investments. That's left the No. 4 economy way behind as 2.0 revs up. Japan's gross domestic product is one-seventh the size of the U.S. Its data center use is one-seventeenth in gigawatt terms, the International Data Center Authority reports.

Investors have plans to fill the gap. Just this month, U.S.-based artificial intelligence A-listers Anthropic and Dell unveiled multibillion-dollar Japanese data center projects, in partnership with NTT and local power generator Jera, respectively. Private-equity giant Blackstone laid out its own $30 billion Japanese agenda in June.

Part of the draw is an emphatic YIMBY attitude from Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government, which flagged AI infrastructure as a priority for the $2.3 trillion, 15-year strategic investment plan it announced this summer. "The government support will be about de-bottlenecking approvals, particularly in power generation," says Noriaki Saito, head of investment strategy at Global X Japan.

What could go wrong? Investors are relaxed about a consensus-oriented Japanese public catching the anti-data center fever that is roiling industry plans from Texas to Australia. "Resistance will probably be limited compared to other countries," predicts Keiichi Matsumoto, director of the government-linked Japan U.S. Venture Ecosystem.

Takaichi has effectively linked keeping data at home with national security as global cyberattacks and AI "accidents" increase. Aberdeen's Arakawa notes. Despite its famous population density, Japan has large tracts of abandoned rural land for data center siting, adds Neil Newman, head of strategy at Tokyo-based Astris Advisory. "More than 90% of Japanese live in urban areas," he says. "Rural areas are so empty, there is no one there to complain."

Japan's more acute challenge in the data center race is power, Newman says. Lacking its own fossil fuel resources, the country was aiming for nuclear power to provide half its electricity before the Fukushima disaster of 2011, he notes. The proportion today is less than 10%, leading to a sort of soft rationing for households. "You can't sell electric vehicles here because there's not enough power to charge them up," Newman says.

Takaichi has plans for a nuclear resurgence in the 2030s. Arakawa is skeptical. "The nuclear restarts have been quite political with local governments getting involved," he says.

While Anthropic and Dell are both aiming for the Tokyo-Osaka metropolitan belt, the northern island of Hokkaido is emerging as a land of the data center future, combining wide open spaces, wind power, and temperatures that minimize cooling costs. SoftBank Group and Toyota Group subsidiary Eurus Energy are among the heavy hitters moving forward there.

Arakawa sees Japanese data center capacity doubling over the next few years, a relatively conservative estimate. That should lift the shares of overlooked electrical engineering contractors like Kraftia and Kandenko, he predicts. "We are seeing double-digit order growth and rapid market expansion in this subsector," he says.

Other Japanese names already play unheralded but critical roles in the global data center supply chain and stand to benefit from domestic expansion. Global X's Saito flags Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, a top producer of turbines for natural gas-powered electricity generators, and Daihen, which makes transformers for power grids. Arakawa adds Daihen competitor Fuji Electric and Sumitomo Electric Industries, a standout manufacturer of the optical cables that thread through data centers.

"As long as the supply chain is paid, all these companies will be fine," Neil Newman comments.

One indication of how fast and far Japan will move on data centers should come by year's end, when a Takaichi budget attaches some concrete yen amounts to her strategic investment priorities, which number no less than 17.

Standing still doesn't seem like an option, though, for a Japan increasingly convinced it needs to stand on its own. "The geopolitical backdrop matters more than a decade or two ago," Saito says. "Having data centers within Japan seems more important nowadays."
